Another untimely injury for Lamar Jackson (thumb) means the NFL DFS player pool is now headlined by Trevor Lawrence and Derrick Henry. Other appealing options for NFL DFS lineups include Bhayshul Tuten and Parker Washington of the Jags, as well as Baltimore's Zay Flowers. A potential sleeper TNF DFS pick is Brian Thomas Jr., who found the end zone on Sunday after back-to-back games without a catch. If you expect the Ravens to struggle offensively without Jackson and settle for field goals instead of touchdowns, then Baltimore's kicker could be a part of your TNF DFS strategy. Additionally, rostering the Jags' No. 2 scoring defense shouldn't be overlooked when constructing a daily Fantasy football strategy versus a Baltimore offense that's scored just one touchdown in each of its last three games. You can only see his picks and analysis at SportsLine . Top NFL DFS picks for Ravens vs. Jags One of McClure's top NFL DFS picks for 'Thursday Night Football' is Baltimore running back Derrick Henry. A native of the Jacksonville area, Henry loves facing his hometown team. He's averaged 129.1 rushing yards with 14 total touchdowns over his last 10 games versus the Jags. With Jackson out, Baltimore should heavily lean on Henry versus a Jacksonville defense which is suddenly susceptible to the run. After allowing just 63.8 rushing yards over the first five games, the Jags have given up 100-plus on the ground in each of the last two. Also, while Henry isn't normally a factor out of the backfield, that could change on Thursday as just five teams allow more receptions per game to RBs than Jacksonville. McClure's also building around Jags RB Bhayshul Tuten who is coming off a career game, setting highs in rushing yards (104), receiving yards (55) and total yards (159) while also scoring twice. Tuten has at least 87 scrimmage yards in all but one game this year and has scored multiple touchdowns in back-to-back weeks. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights A look at where the odds and spreads currently stand heading into Week 9, including a big move in Baltimore Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens will likely have to go the rest of the 2026 regular season without star quarterback Lamar Jackson . The two-time NFL MVP made his return to action on Sunday after a three-game absence due to an ankle injury, but that comeback was very short-lived. On the first play from scrimmage for the Ravens offense, Jackson jammed his right thumb on Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau on a follow-through. That injury not only knocked him out of the game, but head coach Jesse Minter told reporters postgame that Jackson will go on injured reserve and will undergo surgery. On top of this injury turning Baltimore's season upside down, it's also thrown the line for their Week 9 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars for a loop. Not only did Jackson go down on Sunday, but backup Tyler Huntley (toe) also did, and his status for Week 9 is up in the air. That could result in undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano getting the start. With that uncertainty under center, it's no surprise to see the Ravens go from being a 3-point favorite at home to now an 8.5-point home underdog. The total also dropped from 48.5 down to 43.5. This just shows how much a line can swing when a player of Jackson's caliber is sidelined. While we won't see as dramatic of swings throughout the rest of the Week 9 slate, there has been some notable movement that is worth pointing out. So, as we close the book on Week 8, let's take our first glimpse at the upcoming week and who the oddsmakers have coming out on top. Note : Pittsburgh and Tennessee are on the bye in Week 9. Week 9 early odds All lines via DraftKings ; all games on Sunday unless noted Early moneyline Jaguars at Ravens (Thursday) Jaguars -426, Ravens +330 Bengals at Falcons (in Madrid) Bengals -170, Falcons +142 Broncos at Panthers Broncos -155, Panthers +130 Browns at Saints Browns +124, Saints -148 Cowboys at Colts Cowboys -265, Colts +215 Rams at Commanders Rams -225, Commanders +185 Lions at Dolphins Lions -355, Dolphins +280 Jets at Chiefs Jets +380, Chiefs -500 Giants at Eagles Giants -135, Eagles +114 Texans at Chargers Texans -218, Chargers +180 Packers at Patriots Patriots -2.5 Packers +124, Patriots -148 Cardinals at Seahawks Seahawks -11.5 Cardinals +525, Seahawks -752 Raiders at 49ers Raiders +390, 49ers -521 Buccaneers at Bears Buccaneers +205, Bears -250 Bills at Vikings (Monday) Bills -148, Vikings +124 Notable movement, trends As we noted in the intro, the Lamar Jackson injury has nuked this line. Baltimore is now an 8.5-point home underdog to the Jaguars after opening as a field goal favorite. The total also dropped down to 43.5 after opening at 48.5. Jacksonville is 4-3 ATS on the season, which includes a 1-1 ATS record on the road. Amid all of the QB turnover even prior to this latest Jackson injury, the Ravens enter Week 9 0-3 ATS at home. The NFL heads back out into international waters for this matchup between the Bengals and Falcons, this time to Madrid. Cincinnati has opened as a field goal favorite as Joe Burrow and the offense are starting to find their rhythm after the Bengals QB just totaled six touchdowns in a win over Tennessee. Meanwhile, Michael Penix Jr . imploded for the Falcons, throwing four interceptions in a loss to Tampa Bay. The Bengals are 3-4 ATS this season, while the Falcons are 3-5 ATS. The total moved up to 51.5 after opening at 49.5, and the Over is 9-6 combined between these two teams this season. Denver is coming off another comeback win, this time rallying to defeat the Chiefs at home to take over first place in the AFC North. Now, they'll look to win their fifth-straight game when they visit the Panthers. Carolina will have the rest advantage over the Broncos after playing last Thursday, but are home dogs. Denver is laying 3-points as a road favorite. The Broncos' 6-2 ATS record is tied for the best in the NFL, but the club is 2-2 ATS on the road. However, as a road favorite, Denver is 2-0 ATS. As a home underdog, the Panthers are 1-1 ATS entering Week 9. The total sits at 44.5, and the Under is a combined 9-6 between these squads. New Orleans was on the bye in Week 8, so it'll be well-rested when it squares off against the Browns on Sunday. The Saints are a 3-point favorite at home and are still looking for their first ATS victory at the Superdome (0-3 ATS). On the road this season, the Browns are 2-3 ATS. With the total sitting at 43.5, it's worth noting that the Over is 2-1 in Saints home games this season. Dallas has jumped out as a 6-point favorite after the line initially opened Cowboys -4.5. This has more to do with Indy's ongoing implosion and the possibility that it continues to sell off pieces before the deadline. On Sunday, the Colts lost 42-7 to the Jaguars and Daniel Jones was benched. It's unclear if Jones will start in Week 9. If he doesn't, Anthony Richardson would likely get the nod. Dallas is 2-2 ATS on the road, but that includes a 1-2 ATS mark as a road favorite. Indy is 1-2 ATS at Lucas Oil Stadium. The total for this game jumped up to 52.5 after opening at 51.5. The Over is 6-2 in Cowboys games this season. The Rams have quietly stabilized after a 2-4 start to the regular season. They've won two straight to get back to .500 on the year and are now a 5.5-point road favorite as they gear up for a matchup against the Commanders. LA is 4-4 ATS this season, which includes a 2-1 ATS on the road. Both of those ATS road wins came as road favorites. Meanwhile, the Commanders are 1-0 ATS as a home underdog. After handing Minnesota its first loss of the season, the Lions now head down to South Beach as a 7-point road favorite over the Dolphins. Detroit is 1-2 ATS on the road, which includes a 1-1 ATS record as a road favorite. At Hard Rock Stadium, the Dolphins are 2-1 ATS. The total sits at 48.5. Between these two teams this season, the Over is 9-5. Kansas City is now a double-digit favorite over the Jets, laying 10 points after the line opened at 9.5. The Chiefs fell out of first place in the AFC West after allowing the Broncos to score 15 unanswered fourth-quarter points. That said, the Jets shouldn't present the same level of resistance. Kansas City is 2-1 ATS at Arrowhead, while the Jets are 2-1-1 ATS on the road. The total for this game opened at 43.5 but has since moved up to 45.5. The Under is 2-1 in Chiefs home games this season. The Giants were on the bye in Week 8, so they'll be well rested for this NFC East road matchup in Philly. They'll enter Lincoln Financial Field as a 2.5-point favorite, which is up from the 1.5 points they were laying at the open. New York is 5-2 ATS entering Week 9, which includes a 2-1 ATS record on the road. Philadelphia is 0-3 ATS as a home underdog in 2026. Houston picked up a point and a half and are laying 4.5 points on the road to the Chargers after initially opening as a field goal favorite. LA remains winless on the season after falling to the Rams on Sunday. It is 0-1 ATS as a home underdog this season and 0-3 ATS at home overall. The Texans are 1-1 ATS on the road. The total sits at 42.5, and the Under could be a popular play, with it owning a 6-1 record in Chargers games this season. New England is a 2.5-point favorite at home over the Packers, who'll have a rest advantage after playing last Thursday. New England is 3-4-1 ATS this season, which includes a 2-1 ATS record at home. As for the Packers, they're 2-2 ATS on the road this season (5-3 ATS overall). The Under is 3-1 in Packers road games entering Week 9. Seattle is an 11.5-point favorite despite squaring off against Arizona after playing on a short week. Given that the Seahawks still have their Week 8 matchup with the Bears to play on Monday night, this line could see movement once that game goes final. Arizona is coming off an upset win on the road against Dallas, improving to 4-1 ATS on the road this season. One thing worth monitoring with the Cardinals is their situation at quarterback. Jacoby Brissett was benched for Gardner Minshew on Sunday, so it'll be interesting to see how Mike LaFleur approaches the position going forward. San Francisco emerges from the bye week as a 9.5-point favorite over the Raiders. The Niners are 2-2 ATS at home this season with an average margin of victory of 11 points. Meanwhile, the Raiders are 3-1 ATS on the road this season, and that 75% cover rate is tied for the third-highest in the NFL. The total, which sits at 51.5 for this game, is 6-2 in Raiders games this season and 3-4 in Niners games. Chicago still has its Week 8 matchup to play on Monday night, but are 6-point favorites at home over the Bucs. Tampa Bay won on Sunday despite recording zero passing yards and Baker Mayfield attempting just three passes (all incompletions). It's safe to say they'll need to throw it to kee

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 9 picks, including the Bills handing the Vikings their second straight loss Imagn Images The turnaround week looked promising early Sunday. Then it went rotten — at least with my against-the-spread NFL picks , I went into the late games with a 6-3 ATS record. I ended up 7-7 for the week. That takes my season record to a horrible 50-68-3. As for my straight-up picks, I went 10-4. That brings my season record to 72-48-1. That I will take. Now it's time to get going on the ATS record. I went with some strange dogs this week in hopes of getting back on track. Let's hope they bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Jacksonville Jaguars (-10) at Baltimore Ravens Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Jaguars get a break on a short week, not having to face Lamar Jackson at quarterback. The Ravens are a different team without him and now must play rookie Joe Fagnano . Trevor Lawrence is playing at a high level and the run game is going well. Look for the Jaguars to win a road game on a short week. Pick: Jaguars 27, Ravens 16 Cincinnati Bengals (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Madrid on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals have been flying high on offense with Joe Burrow throwing it around. The Falcons have struggled on offense in recent weeks, which is never a good thing when trying to keep up with Burrow. Look for a lot more big plays from the Bengals as they win this one in Spain. Pick: Bengals 33, Falcons 21 Denver Broncos (-2.5) at Carolina Panthers Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Panthers have been beat up the past two games, leading to the firing of defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero. They are reeling on defense. The Broncos won a tough one last week against the Chiefs thanks to late-game magic by Bo Nix . This time, it's a lot easier against a bad Panthers defense and struggling offensive line. Pick: Broncos 26, Panthers 20 Dallas Cowboys (-6) at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys are coming off a horrible loss to the Cardinals at home, but they get a big break playing the Colts , who are struggling. Indianapolis has major problems and there is talk of trading more players. The Cowboys will get the offense cranked up again in this one as they get back on track behind their passing game. Pick: Cowboys 31, Colts 17 New York Jets (+9.5) at Kansas City Chiefs The Chiefs are back home after losing two straight on the road. The Jets blew a late lead to the Raiders last week. Kansas City has not run it the past two weeks, but look for Kenneth Walker to get back on track. The Chiefs win it to break the losing streak, but the Jets and their offense hang around. Pick: Chiefs 24, Jets 17 Detroit Lions (-7) at Miami Dolphins This is a tough trip for the Lions coming off two home division victories, and it's against a young team playing much better. But this is a big challenge for the Miami defense. The Lions can score in bunches and I think they will in this one. Look for a big day from Jared Goff . Pick: Lions 30, Dolphins 13 Cleveland Browns at New Orleans Saints (-1.5) The Browns are playing consecutive road games after losing to the Steelers last week. The Saints are coming off a bye, so big advantage there. The Browns were bad on offense against the Steelers, which I think carries over here. The Saints will do enough to win a low-scoring game. Pick: Saints 17, Browns 14 New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles (+3.5) The Giants are coming off a bye in first place in the division, while the Eagles are coming off a road loss Sunday night to the Commanders . They are struggling in many areas. But this is a big rivalry, and pride will help keep the Eagles in it, as their defense has a solid day against J.J. McCarthy . But the Giants win it late. Pick: Giants 22, Eagles 20 Los Angeles Rams at Washington Commanders (+5.5) This is a long trip for the Rams , but they seemed to have righted things the past few weeks. The Commanders rallied to beat the Eagles Sunday night. The Washington defense played well in that game, but this could be a game where Matt Stafford gets it cranked up. Jayden Daniels will play well to keep it close, but the Rams will win it. Pick: Rams 28, Commanders 24 Houston Texans at Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Texans are coming off a bye, while the Chargers are coming off a loss to the Rams. Neither team has come close to expectations before the season, with the Chargers winless. The Texans' defense and the Chargers' offense have both struggled. But I think the Chargers will hang around in this one behind their defense. Pick: Texans 19, Chargers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at San Francisco 49ers (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, while the 49ers are coming off a bye. Big edge for the 49ers. Plus, they are the better team. The Raiders' defense is struggling, so look for Brock Purdy to have a big day throwing the football. 49ers big. Pick: 49ers 31, Raiders 17 Green Bay Packers at New England Patriots (+3.5) This has the feel of a low-scoring game with two good defenses — even though both teams have good quarterbacks. The Packers have added rest from playing last Thursday, which will help. The Patriots had to rally and beat the Dolphins last week. The defenses play well, but It's Jordan Love who makes the plays late to win it. Pick: Packers 19, Patriots 16 Arizona Cardinals at Seattle Seahawks (-12.5) The Seahawks are coming off an embarrassing home loss to the Bears , while the Cardinals won at Dallas last week. They are making a quarterback change to Gardner Minshew , who played well last week. Good luck against this Seattle defense, which will be hunting after the Bears beat them. The Cardinals will get the brunt of their anger. Pick: Seahawks 30, Cardinals 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are coming off that impressive victory over Seattle Monday night on the road. That was domination. But there might be a little letdown here. The Bucs have played impressive defense this season and have cranked up their running game. They will run it well here, but in the end, Caleb Williams will make late plays to win it. Pick: Bears 24, Bucs 21 Buffalo Bills (-3.5) at Minnesota Vikings Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the game of the week, featuring two of the better teams in the league. I can't wait to see the Vikings ' defense against Josh Allen . But I think the Bills will run the ball at the Minnesota defense, much like the Lions did last week. The Bills defense has been better as of late, and that will show up against a limited Minnesota offense. picks.headline: Jaguars vs. Ravens Odds Continue to Shift Towards Jacksonville With Joe Fagnano Set to Start in NFL Week 9
picks.blurb: Jaguars vs. Ravens Odds Continue to Shift Towards Jacksonville With Joe Fagnano Set to Start in NFL Week 9 Skip to main content ON SI PREDICTION MARKETS Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Things keep getting worse for the Baltimore Ravens at quarterback, as they've lost Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury and Tyler Huntley (turf toe) is done for the season. That has put third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano in line to start in Week 9 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, which has caused a massive move in the odds. Sources: tests revealed that Ravens’ QB Tyler “Snoop” Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury. Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is out indefinitely with a thumb injury, Huntley’s season is over due to turf toe, and QB Joe Fagnano will start Thursday night vs. Jacksonville. pic.twitter.com/Cok4gbSvH3 Baltimore was favored in the lookahead line for this game before Week 8 with Jackson back in action, but the two-time league MVP was injured on the first offensive play for Baltimore and has since been ruled out for the next four weeks as he's set to go on injured reserve. So, the line re-opened with Jacksonville as a 7.5-point favorite on Sunday night. Now, that line has moved 2.5 more points with Huntley out and Fagnano (ankle) set to start. DraftKings Sportsbook has the Jaguars set as 10-point road favorites as they look to move to 6-2 this season. picks.blurb: Jaguars vs. Ravens bold predictions for Week 9 Thursday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Jaguars vs. Ravens bold predictions for Week 9 Thursday Night Football Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 10:16 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's a strange injury-marred matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Baltimore Ravens . It's especially tough as the Ravens got hit at the QB position . But these teams meet in Week 9 on Thursday Night Football, and here are bold predictions. Life is better for the Jaguars. They're in the weaker AFC South division. They have a record of 5-2 and a three-game lead over the second-place Texans. Meanwhile, the Ravens are 4-4. That's worth last place in the tougher AFC North. It's a desperation game for the Ravens. Can they come up with a plan to move the football? Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten will rush for 100-plus yards The Ravens have a fairly solid run defense. But there's a caveat to this prediction. The Jaguars won't need a lot of points to win this game. The Ravens will struggle to put points on the board as the Jaguars stack the box against Derrick Henry. That means the Jaguars will be content to pound the ground game once they get a double-digit lead. And that means more carries for Tuten. He's coming off a 104-yard rushing performance against the Colts. And he should hit the mark again. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he liked what he saw from Tuten, according to jacksonville.com. "I thought Tuten played really well (against the Colts)," Coen said. "He was seeing it. I thought he was a little more patient in this game. He was running through contact. He was explosive in the passing game. Tuten had a great week of practice, and it really carried over." Tuten said things fell into place , according to ESPN. "We knew it was going to rain," Tuten said. "We knew we were going to run the ball, and we just went out and imposed our will." Things are set up nicely for Tuten to have another big game. Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence will throw three TD passes Even if Tuten runs up and down the field, the Ravens will commit to stopping him inside the 10-yard line. That will open up opportunities for Lawrence to complete drives with TD passes. This season, Lawrence has 17 touchdown passes with four interceptions. And Lawrence is trying to keep the Jaguars in all-business mode , according to news4jax.com. "Winning your division is really important, but I think for us, it's really just going week by week," Lawrence said. "It's not something we think, 'Oh, we're a few games up. We're in a good spot. We can relax.' That's not really at all how we think. We got a lot of football left." The Ravens have two choices on defense. They can take chances and try to create splash plays. Or they can sit back and try to keep the game close, where they could steal one in the fourth quarter. If they take chances against Lawrence, he will simply hit them with longer strikes. It seems like a no-win situation for the Ravens. And a big day for Lawrence and the Jaguars. Ravens RB Derrick Henry will set season high in carries Make no doubt about it. The Ravens are going to put a saddle on Henry and try to ride him to a victory. Henry has 24 carries twice this year. But his season high of 26 came against the Cowboys in overtime. Look for him to eclipse that number. That is, if the Ravens can keep the ball long enough for him to rack up carries while the game is still within reach. But it's possible the Ravens will feed Henry even if they fall behind by two scores. That's all because the only real path to a win is through Henry. Henry has been the recent subject of trade rumors because of the injury to Jackson. The Giants have been in that conversation, but head coach John Harbaugh said it's hard to make big trades , according to Giants.com. "We're going to do the most we can possibly do to try to get some things done," Harbaugh said. "It's hard to get deals done. It's hard. You can see how hard it is, but we're going to do our best and what's for our team. And the best thing we can do, the main thing we're going to do is focus on our guys and get ready to play the game. But all that other stuff is definitely going on behind the scenes at all times." For now, Henry remains with the Ravens. And he has to be their leader on Thursday night. He'd be the player expected to lead the Jaguars in rushing yardage with no Tuten. The Jags also don't mind giving Abdullah carries, and if Tuten was out, Abdullah might see some play on offense, too. The Jaguars wouldn't have to elevate Taylor to the active roster Thursday if Tuten is out, but he'd be the one other option they have in the building if they want to stick with their routine of having four RBs active on gameday. Tuten appeared to roll either his foot or ankle early in Sunday's blowout win of the Colts . It didn't stop Tuten from playing the rest of the game. Allen might see a small increase in carries, and he'd also project for a bit more work as a receiver, which is an area Tuten has done more of himself this season. He signed with the Jaguars' practice squad to try and work his way toward a 53-man roster. The 5-foot-9 Taylor played at North Carolina Central and then Virginia in his college career. The status of Jacksonville Jaguars' RB Bhayshul Tuten in Thursday's matchup with the Baltimore Ravens is up in the air at this time. The good news is that after Tuten missed the last two days of practice with ankle and foot injuries, head coach Liam Coen said that he expects him to do "something" on Wednesday, according to Mia O'Brien. The improvements provide some much-needed optimism for a Ravens team dealing with significant injuries during a short week. home.headline: Report: Ravens QB Tyler Huntley (turf toe) out for season
home.blurb: Coming in after Lamar Jackson injured his thumb on the Ravens' first offensive play last Sunday against the Buffalo Bills, Huntley came out of the game in the second quarter when he was sacked, lost a fumble and injured his right foot. The Ravens signed Austin Reed to the practice squad on Monday and inked fellow quarterback Kedon Slovis off the Green Bay Packers' practice squad on Tuesday to round out a depth chart dented by multiple injuries. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Tyler Huntley will miss the remainder of the season due to a turf toe injury, ESPN reported Wednesday morning. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano relieved Huntley and sustained an injury to his right ankle before finishing the game for the Ravens (4-4). He wore a brace on his right ankle during Tuesday's practice, and head coach Jesse Minter later declared that Fagnano will make his first career NFL start on Thursday against the visiting Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2). Jackson, a two-time NFL MVP, is headed to injured reserve and could miss the rest of the season. Signed to a two-year, $5 million contract with up to $6 million in incentives, Huntley has spent six of his seven NFL seasons with the Ravens, who first signed him as an undrafted free agent in 2020. The Miami Dolphins claimed him off the Ravens' practice squad in 2024, and he re-signed with the Ravens in 2025. Huntley, 28, has thrown for 727 yards with four touchdowns and one interception in five games (three starts) this season. He's also rushed for 76 yards and a score. A Pro Bowl selection in 2022, Huntley has appeared in 35 games (19 starts), completing 66.7% of his passes for 3,939 yards, 17 touchdowns and 11 interceptions. He has six rushing touchdowns and 871 yards on the ground. Want more articles like this? Follow Field Level Media on MSN to see more of our exclusive NFL content. home.blurb: Slovis, 25, was the Arizona Cardinals’ backup last season and appeared in two games after Kyler Murray suffered a season-ending foot injury. A former undrafted free agent out of BYU in 2024, he attempted just two passes. Jackson suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens’ first offensive play in Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills and did not return. Coach Jesse Minter said Jackson will undergo surgery on the potentially season-ending injury and will be placed on injured reserve, meaning he will miss at least the next four games. Huntley entered the game but lasted only a few more series before suffering what has been reported as turf toe. Minter did not have an update on Huntley’s status or how long he could be out. Depending on the severity of the injury, Huntley could be sidelined for a couple of weeks or several months. With Lamar Jackson headed to injured reserve and uncertainty over how long backup Tyler Huntley will be sidelined, the Ravens continued adding to their quarterback room on Tuesday. Baltimore signed Kedon Slovis from the Green Bay Packers’ practice squad to its 53-man roster, the team announced. He joins undrafted rookie free agent Joe Fagnano, who will start Thursday night against the Jacksonville Jaguars. He also previously worked with Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork, who held the same position in Arizona. Ravens wide receivers coach Keary Colbert was also with Slovis during the quarterback’s time at USC — Slovis played for the Trojans and Pittsburgh before ending his college career at BYU. The move comes a day after Baltimore also signed Austin Reed to its practice squad. The Ravens (4-4) have lost their last three games and are in last place in the AFC North. home.headline: Ravens Get Disappointing Injury Update on Tyler Huntley After Loss to Bills: Report
home.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens had a rough afternoon, starting with the first offensive play of the game when quarterback Lamar Jackson hit Bills defender Greg Rousseau's arm, causing Jackson to suffer a thumb injury and not return. Jackson's backup, Tyler Huntley , also didn't last long. Huntley suffered a toe injury in the first half and didn't return. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Sunday that Huntley suffered a turf toe injury. Huntley and Jackson could both miss time, and Jackson is confirmed out for at least four weeks. Head coach Jesse Minter said postgame that Jackson will be placed on injured reserve and will undergo surgery on his right thumb. Ravens Get Disappointing Injury Update on Tyler Huntley After Loss to Bills: Report Unlock the latest Heavy on Ravens news — direct to your inbox. This was Jackson first game back after he suffered an ankle injury against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4 and missed the last three games. "Ravens QB Tyler "Snoop" Huntley suffered what is thought to be a turf toe injury today at Buffalo, per source," Schefter wrote on X. "He is expected to undergo an MRI tomorrow to determine how much time if any he could miss." Ravens Could Be Down Jackson and Huntley for a While The Ravens turned to quarterback Joe Fagnano after losing Huntley, and he had a tough afternoon, completing 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards and one interception. Minter also said, "We'll see" on whether Jackson will miss the rest of the season. Huntley has started three games this season, and the Ravens are 1-2. The Ravens beat the Falcons in his first start of the season but lost the last two against the Browns and Bengals. Losing your starting quarterback and backup in the same game is never good. It's even worse when this happens during a short week. The Ravens will have a quick turnaround as they host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night. The Jaguars are coming off a 42-7 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday to move to 5-2. Baltimore might not have a chance to play Huntley even if he can go, since it's hard to come back from an injury on a shorter week with less than four full days to recover. It will also be difficult for the Ravens to bring in a quarterback to play on Thursday, even if they lack confidence in Fagnano. The Ravens might have to get by with Fagnano starting on Thursday, then reevaluate options when they have about 10 days off between their games against the Jaguars and the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16. The Cincinnati Bengals needed a spectacular performance from Joe Burrow to escape with an overtime victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but oddsmakers aren’t expecting the same kind of offensive fireworks when Cincinnati faces the Atlanta Falcons next weekend. Still, with the Bengals’ defense continuing to struggle, the early betting lines suggest another potentially high-scoring affair. That sets up an intriguing matchup between a Falcons offense that couldn’t find the end zone and a Bengals defense that had difficulty keeping the Titans out of it. Update, Nov 3: The Bengals have moved from -3.5 to -3 (-115), and the total has gone up from 51.5 to 52.5. We’re sticking with both picks, graded at the numbers we published (Bengals -3.5, Under 51.5). The moneyline is now live, with the Bengals at -165. Odds from BetOnline as of Nov 3. The Bengals didn’t score in the first quarter and trailed 13-0, before Joe Burrow took over. He went 38 of 48 for 462 yards and five touchdowns, although he also threw three interceptions and lost a fumble, so it wasn’t a clean day. Tee Higgins was the standout, with 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns. That followed a 35-13 win over the Ravens in Week 7, and at 5-2, the Bengals’ offense is as dangerous as any in the league when Burrow gets going. The concern is on the other side of the ball. Cincinnati gave up 36 points to a 1-7 Titans team, with Cameron Ward throwing for 304 yards and Tony Pollard running for 117 yards and two scores. Atlanta’s 16-0 loss in Tampa Bay is a hard game to read too much into. The rain was so heavy that the Buccaneers didn’t complete a single pass, with Baker Mayfield going 0 for 3, and Tampa Bay simply handed the ball to Bucky Irving, who ran for 170 yards and a touchdown. Michael Penix Jr. struggled badly in the conditions, going 8 of 24 for 125 yards with four interceptions, and Bijan Robinson was held to 76 yards on 19 carries. At 3-5, the Falcons need a performance. Sunday’s forecast in Madrid is for some light rain, nothing like last week’s downpour, so Penix should get a fairer chance to throw the ball. Still, this is an offense that has to prove it can score consistently, and Atlanta’s run defense will have questions to answer after the way Irving ran through it. A 9:30 AM ET kickoff plays its part, with both teams adjusting to a body clock that feels like mid-afternoon in Europe and early morning back home. We saw last week how slowly the Bengals can start, with no points in the first quarter, and even light rain can take a little off both passing games. I took the under at 51.5, and the move to 52.5 only gives anyone betting it now an extra point to work with. away.blurb: Kyle Dugger (quad) continues to not practice as he heads toward another missed game this week. Bengals Injury Report: Ja'Marr Chase's Status Upgraded on Thursday as Bengals Continue Titans Preparation Skip to main content SI.COM The Bengals dropped their Thursday injury report ahead of the Titans game, and Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) got upgraded to full status on the report after not practicing due to that small issue and rest in general on Wednesday. He told the media on Thursday his ankle feels fine. Cincinnati is pretty clean besides those names. Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor has had to shuffle around his tight end room due to all of the injuries in recent weeks. Erick All just went on season-ending injured reserve with a torn ACL, and fellow tight end Tanner Hudson tore a pec this season as well. "Attention to detail has been really important to him," Taylor said about rookie tight end Jack Endries as he gets primed for more snaps. "Waiting for his moment, you can tell he never knew when his number was going to be called. He's really got to know three different positions and so I've got trust, just watching him operate in practice and in meetings and in training camp, that if needed, he was going to be ready to go, and there was a time where he wasn't needed because we had everybody healthy, and now's that time. So I'm not nervous at all about using him. I think he's earning the opportunity. I'm excited to watch him play." Taylor also echoed confidence in backup safety PJ Jules, who is filling in for Dugger's reserve role. "PJ brings a lot of energy. It's really important to him," Taylor noted. "He's done a great job on special teams in his roles. He stepped into safety. So when we need to continue to rely on depth at the safety position, I feel very confident in PJ and Russ (Yeast)." away.blurb: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans Skip to content The Cincinnati Bengals released their third and final injury report ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati has officially declared one player out, and another questionable for Sunday's game against Tennessee. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is officially out, and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is officially questionable against the Titans. Coach Zac Taylor said at the beginning of the week Dugger would not play and is “week-to-week” after aggravating his calf injury last week against the Baltimore Ravens. Giles-Harris figures to be a game-time decision, and his status may be foreshadowed depending on whether or not the club elevates LB Emany Johnson off the practice squad Saturday. As expected, Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is good to play despite missing Wednesday. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill, and Dexter Lawrence II all had standard rest days. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) have all been declared out. None of them practiced at all this week, including Tate, the former Ohio State Buckeye and No. 4 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable. Assuming he plays, it'll be him, Elic Ayomanor, and Wan'Dale Robinson leading quarterback Cam Ward's passing attack with Tate sidelined. Starting tight end Gunnar Helm may also see a rise in involvement. He caught four passes for 24 yards last week against the Cleveland Browns. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) is also questionable, along with cornerback Jaylon Jones (knee), and LB Dorian Mausi (foot). Mausi is still on the Reserve/Injured list and is ineligible to play unless Tennessee activates him to its 53-man roster. The Cincinnati Bengals are riding high after their second consecutive victory. They'll look to make it three in a row as they return home to face the Tennessee Titans. Mayfield guided the Bucs to their second win of the season against the Carolina Panthers in Week 7, and oddsmakers are buying the Buccaneers at home in Week 8 against the Atlanta Falcons. The Buccaneers are favored to win their matchup with the Falcons, sitting as 2.5-point favorites in the odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . After a 1-5 start to the season, Tampa Bay's win over Carolina thrust it back into the mix to win the division this season. Another win over an NFC South opponent would go a long way for Tampa Bay getting into the playoffs, and the running game has really stepped forward in recent weeks with both Mayfield and Jalon Daniels under center. Mayfield wasn't asked to do much against Carolina, completing just seven of his 11 passes for 76 yards and a score. He's completed 63.6 percent of his passes for 679 yards, three scores and two picks in four games. Daniels led Tampa Bay to one win while Mayfield was sidelined, but it's pretty clear that oddsmakers view the former No. 1 overall pick as a major upgrade under center. Mayfield and the Bucs take on Altanta and Chicago over the next two weeks before their bye. Atlanta is currently one game ahead of Tampa Bay in the NFC South, but a win on Sunday would vault the Bucs into second in the divison, just a half-game back of the Panthers (3-4). home.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Dallas Cowboys Have Been Scoring but Giving Up Too Much Dallas is 3-5 after losing 33-30 to Arizona in overtime on Sunday. That’s a frustrating way to lose, especially when you’ve scored 30 points at home. The Cowboys had beaten Philadelphia 38-21 the previous week, so the offense has been doing its job lately. Sixty-eight points in two games should be enough to win both. Instead, Dallas split them. The problem is the defense. You can’t keep giving up big plays and expecting the offense to bail you out. Arizona moved the ball well enough to score 33, and now Dallas is heading into another road game. Indianapolis hasn’t been particularly dangerous offensively, but the Cowboys have made life easier for opponents who probably shouldn’t be scoring as much as they are. Still, I like Dallas’ chances of moving the football Sunday. The Cowboys have scored at least 30 points in consecutive games, and Indianapolis just got embarrassed by Jacksonville. If Dallas gets into a rhythm early, the Colts could have a difficult time keeping up. That’s especially true if Indianapolis has to abandon its running game and start chasing points. Indianapolis Colts Need to Forget About Jacksonville Indianapolis is 2-6 after losing 42-7 to Jacksonville last Sunday. If Indianapolis can run the football, keep the game close, and avoid turnovers, it might be able to hang around. But after scoring seven against Jacksonville, I’m not ready to trust the Colts to do enough offensively. I don’t love backing a 3-5 team on the road, but Indianapolis has been even worse. The Colts just lost by 35 points and have scored only 17 over their last two games. Dallas, meanwhile, has scored 68 in its last two. That’s a pretty significant difference. The Cowboys’ defense worries me, and I wouldn’t be surprised if Indianapolis finds some success against it. But I think Dallas has enough offense to pull away. Give me the Cowboys by a touchdown or more. Total Pick: Over 51.5 I’ll take the over 51.5, but this one comes with some risk. Dallas has been involved in some high-scoring games lately, and its defense just gave up 33 to Arizona. The Cowboys can probably get into the 30s against Indianapolis, which gives us a good start. The question is whether the Colts can contribute enough. Scoring seven against Jacksonville doesn’t inspire confidence, but Dallas has been allowing opponents to move the football. If Indianapolis gets into the low 20s, I think we have a good chance. Something like 34-21 would get us there. home.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. home.blurb: Cornerback Justin Walley (knee) missed practice today. Walley was a game time decision in Sunday with the knee injury but managed to play and looked excellent. home.headline: Colts' injury report includes good news on Tyler Warren, Sauce Gardner, bad news on Justin Walley
home.blurb: Starting outside cornerback Sauce Gardner is set to return after missing time with a calf injury. Starting tight end Tyler Warren will also return to play after being sidelined for two games with a groin injury. Indianapolis will be without starting slot corner Justin Walley , who suffered a knee injury late in Sunday’s road loss to the Vikings and did not practice this week, as well as the team’s first corner off the bench, veteran Cam Taylor-Britt , who landed on injured reserve this week with a groin injury also suffered late in Sunday’s 16-10 loss. The Colts will also get back starting tight end Tyler Warren , who missed the team’s last two games with a groin injury. Warren logged his first practice of any kind Thursday after suffering the injury Oct. 23 before a Week 6 game against the Titans where he didn’t appear as a game-time decision. Warren, the team’s leader in catches (30), missed all of last week’s practice, too, as well as the Week 7 game. He was limited in Thursday’s practice but then participated fully Friday. Along with Walley, the Colts also ruled out wide receiver Anthony Gould for Sunday’s game as the return specialist continues to work his way back from a concussion suffered in Week 6. Gould returned to practice this week and was full both days but needs to clear the league’s concussion protocol. Tight end Drew Ogletree (knee) and Bryce Boettcher (groin) are listed as questionable for Sunday’s game. Ogletree was limited in Thursday’s practice and then did not participate Friday, and Boettcher missed both outings after practicing once last week but missing Sunday’s Week 7 game. With Boettcher’s role Sunday in question, all signs point to rookie linebacker C.J. Allen making his first start of his NFL career, as he returns from an ankle injury he suffered last week in practice that sidelined him Sunday. Allen was a full participant in both the Colts’ practices this week. In Week 9, our team is looking to two teams that are favored by six or more points, including Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs after a tough loss at the hands of the Denver Broncos in Week 8. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 9 Survivor Pool Picks Kansas City Chiefs The Kansas City Chiefs have some issues finishing drives when they take on the elite teams in the NFL, but based on their running game and defense alone, they're well-suited to crush inferior teams. They'll host the New York Jets in Week 9, who can't beat the likes of the Miami Dolphins or Las Vegas Raiders. The Jets' defense has been especially bad this season, ranking 24th in opponent success rate. It's also worth noting that Kansas City doesn't have many more games this season that will make sense for Survivor. A home game against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11 is the other option, but at this point, I believe in the Jets a lot less than Arizona. The Chiefs may not be as explosive as they once were, but on their home field they'll cruise past the Jets and help us advance our survivor entries to Week 10. – Iain MacMillan Dallas Cowboys I know the Dallas Cowboys and their terrible defense absolutely crushed Survivor Players (including our own Iain MacMillan) in Week 8, but I’m willing to go back to them on the road in a must-win game against the Indianapolis Colts. Indy was blown out by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8 – 42-7 – and it’s a candidate to move on from more pieces ahead of the trade deadline. The Colts haven’t been a competitive team for most of this season, starting with a 2-6 record while ranking 29th in EPA/Play on offense and 23rd in EPA/Play on defense. The Dallas defense can’t stop anyone, ranking 32nd in EPA/Play and 30th in yards per play allowed, but this offense is still elite. The Cowboys put up 30 points once again in Week 8 against Arizona, and they’re a top-10 team in EPA/Play and success rate on that side of the ball. Dak Prescott should be able to move the ball pretty easily against a Colts defense that couldn’t slow down Trevor Lawrence (three passing scores) and the Jaguars in Week 8. Indy is an easy team to fade the rest of the season with Daniel Jones clearly in over his head at quarterback. Jones has five touchdown passes, nine picks and has only completed 60.4 percent of his passes. If Dallas can’t win this game, the NFC East crown may truly be out of reach. I’ll take the Cowboys – who are six-point road favorites – to bounce back on Sunday. – Peter Dewey Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. Last week the Jets lost at home against the previously winless Miami Dolphins. This week the Las Vegas Raiders broke their own four game losing streak by out-scoring the Jets in a wild 38 – 33 shootout in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Jets took a nine point lead into the locker room at halftime, only to unravel in the second half. The Jets defense was helpless to stop the Raiders attack in the second half as the Jets were out-scored 24 – 10 to close the game. It was a humiliating performance by a putrid Jets defense. The embarrassing Jets loss left the Jets with a 2-6 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Any hopes of a playoff run are all but gone. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. Now the Jets go on the road to face the 5-2 Kansas City Chiefs in Kansas City next Sunday. The Chiefs have lost two straight games to tough opponents on the road. This week the Denver Broncos barely survived as the Chiefs were stopped on the one yard line as they were trying for a game winning score as time ran out. The Chiefs opened the 2026 season with a dominant 31 – 10 victory over the Denver Broncos. They followed that impressive win with four straight victories over some of the worst teams in the NFL – the Indianapolis Colts, Miami Dolphins, Las Vegas Raiders and Los Angeles Chargers. The 5-0 start to the season was great, but with four of the wins coming against bad teams, it is tough to say just how good the Chiefs are. Now they have lost two straight to tough opponents. Are the Chiefs a top team? Maybe. It's not entirely clear. What is crystal clear is the Chiefs are a far, far better team than the Jets. Teams like the Dolphins and the Raiders have snapped their losing streaks against the Jets in East Rutherford. It seems all but inevitable Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs will do the same at home. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Unsurprisingly the oddsmakers think the Chiefs will easily handle the Jets. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 9.5 points. The game has an over/under of 46.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +400 while the Chiefs are -520. Any given Sunday and all that jazz, but an upset here seems like a bridge too far for the Jets. Perhaps they can at least pull off one of those infamous moral victories and keep the game competitive against a Chiefs team that may understandably have trouble getting up for a game against the hapless Jets. The Jets are coming off a frustrating 38-33 home loss to the Raiders in which they produced plenty of offense but couldn’t stop Vegas late. New York scored on its first six possessions, led 23-14 at halftime and 30-21 during the third quarter, but Las Vegas rallied with back-to-back touchdown drives to take a lead late. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, while Braelon Allen rushed for a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown and Adonai Mitchell produced a career-best 142 receiving yards with a score. A big red flag for the Jets continues to be their inefficiency in the red zone on offense and defense: New York went just 2-for-6 in the red zone while Las Vegas finished 4-for-4. Kansas City also melted late in their game last Sunday against the Broncos, blowing a 24-13 fourth-quarter lead in a 28-24 loss at Denver. Patrick Mahomes played much better than he had in the Chiefs’ previous defeat at Seattle, completing 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, including a 73-yard touchdown to Emmett Johnson . Denver, however, scored 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal, and after Mahomes drove the Chiefs inside the Broncos’ 5 in the final minute, Denver made a goal-line stand capped by Malcolm Roach’s sack on fourth down. Historically, the matchup has produced some memorable games. The most recent meeting was a few years ago on October 1, 2023, when Kansas City escaped MetLife Stadium with a 23-20 win. Mahomes had an unusually uneven passing night, finishing 18 of 30 for 203 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, but Kansas City retook the lead on Butker’s 26-yard field goal and Mahomes used his legs to help drain the clock late. The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they’ve strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. Nov 2 (Reuters) - Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital, the NFL team said on Monday, a day after he was carried off the field with a frightening injury during a game against the Minnesota Vikings. Campbell lay motionless on the ground after levelling a hit on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson early in the fourth quarter at Ford Field and was taken to hospital after medical staff removed him from the field. The Pro Bowl linebacker, a captain for the team this season, was drafted by the Lions in the first round three years ago and coach Dan Campbell described him as the consummate teammate. "You get voted captain, that says a ton," said coach Campbell. "He earned every bit of that. He's trustworthy, he's dependable, he'd give you the shirt off his back. He's just all heart, man, all effort." (Reporting by Amy Tennery in New YorkEditing by Christian Radnedge)

away.headline: Detroit Lions injury update: Kerby Joseph won't play vs. Dolphins
away.blurb: A third-round pick in 2022 out of Illinois, Joseph led the NFL in interceptions during the 2024 season with nine picks. In his career, Joseph has played in 55 games and started 52, totaling 20 interceptions, 35 passes defensed, 265 tackles, two tackles for loss, and two quarterback hits. In his Tuesday radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket's "Costa and Jansen with Heather," Lions head coach Dan Campbell was asked for an update on safety Kerby Joseph's progress. Campbell said Joseph won't play this week for the Lions at the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. "Kerby will be in practice this week. We're going to try to give him some scout team reps. He's not going to play this game. So, I know that was coming. He's not playing versus Miami. He's just going to get some reps in practice," Campbell said of Joseph. The Lions opened Joseph's 21-day practice window last Wednesday on Oct. 28. The 6-foot, 210-pound All-Pro safety has been rehabbing a cartilage issue in his knee . Joseph last played in an NFL game on Oct. 12, 2025, against the Kansas City Chiefs . Campbell shared several other injury updates as well, saying that Detroit is preparing as though Juice Scruggs may start at center with starting center Cade Mays banged up again. "Look, Cade has got this ankle right now. What I would say is that Juice came in and played very well. That's what I would definitely say. Juice, he took the mental reps this week. He got a couple live, but really it was more of the mental (reps) at center. To get thrust back in there against that defense with everything they were doing and to have the production, it was impressive and he was locked in. He was so ready to go. "I've told you this before. We love Juice. He just fits us and he's all about business. He's a great teammate, he's high energy. He tries to finish plays, runs off the football. So, he did a heck of a job. As of right now, he's our guy, because I don't see Cade practicing Wednesday and he might not Thursday. So, we're going to get Juice ready to go here," Campbell said. Safety Brian Branch and EDGE DJ Wonnum remain in concussion protocol, starting cornerback D.J. Reed has a hip injury, and running back Jacob Saylors left Sunday's game with a neck injury. "BB and Wonnum, they're in concussion protocol, so we won't know. We'll know where we're at in Phase 1 of this thing today, or later this afternoon. Reed's got a hip. There again, it doesn't look good for him on Wednesday for sure. Until I can get more on that, I don't see where he's at... I don't see Saylors on Wednesday. "That's kind of where we're at. We did, we took a little bit of a hit here. We knew it was coming. I mean, it's fortunate we got this far. So, that's the good news. We actually got a little bit further this time, and we'll adjust. We've got plenty of guys. We've got football players, and we'll adjust," Campbell said. For more Lions coverage, follow us on X, @TheLionsWire , and give our Facebook page a like . home.headline: Final Dolphins-Pats Injury Report: Proctor News Ends Remarkable Streak, Brown Remains a Mystery
home.blurb: Their season-opening streak of games with the same starting offensive line will end at six with the official Friday that rookie first-round pick Kadyn Proctor had been ruled out of the Week 8 game against the New England Patriots because of his concussion. This pretty much was a foregone conclusion once Proctor sat out practice Wednesday and Thursday, and it became official after he once again was a DNP on Friday. Proctor was the only member of the active roster who did not practice Friday and the only one who was so much as limited was long-snapper Tucker Addington, who continues to deal with a shoulder injury. Cornerback JuJu Brents was one of two players listed as questionable, but after being a full participant Friday, two days after missing practice with a concussion, it's a matter of getting final clearance over the weekend to play against New England and the outlook clearly is promising. Also listed as questionable was cornerback Reese Taylor, who has missed the past three games with a quad injury. Taylor had his first full practice in weeks Friday, though it should be pointed out that final practice of the week always is pretty light. New England didn't rule out anybody, which kind of comes as a bit of a surprise given the late-week developments involving wide receiver A.J. Brown. "Just like everything else, when you come out of the game or a long week or practice on Monday, you evaluate the player," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said. "He just wasn't able to practice or finish practice on Wednesday. So, we’ll continue to treat him, and then we'll see where he is (Saturday)." Running back TreVeyon Henderson missed practice for a second consecutive day because of illness and was listed as questionable, as were CB Carlton Davis III (neck) and LB Christian Elliss (chest). That season, the Dolphins opened with a starting five of (from left to right) Laremy Tunsil, Anthony Steen, Mike Pouncey, Jermon Bushrod and Ja'Wuan James until Steen was replaced by Jesse Davis in the seventh game. Since then, the Dolphins hadn't even gone five games at the start of a season with the same offensive line, reaching four games in 2020. And Dolphins fans surely remember last year when the Dolphins lost both James Daniels and Austin Jackson in the opener. So, yes, six games together for Patrick Paul, Proctor, Aaron Brewer, Jonah Savaiinaea and Jackson indeed was a big deal. Watson took a big hit in the first quarter of Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, but he was cleared to return to the game. The New Orleans Saints seem to be heading straight toward a running back trade before the NFL's trading deadline of Tuesday, Nov. 10. At this point, it seems to be more about which RB is the one that actually gets traded from a crowded room of Travis Etienne, Alvin Kamara , Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson . If you're assuming that Etienne isn't going anywhere, you'd be right — he signed a four-year contract in the offseason to be the RB1 and has no indications from any reports that he'll be traded. Both Miller and Kamara have been mentioned in a new report on Saturday that could point to what comes next. The Athletic's Jonathan Jones reported Saturday morning that as long as Etienne is healthy, Miller could be moved. To be fair to Miller, he has looked a little more effective this season in the absence of Etienne. But if the Saints can cash in on some value for him, it could be worth doing. Kamara is a franchise legend who has only ever played in the NFL for New Orleans. He took a paycut in the offseason to stick around. This is what Jones reported about Kamara: Multiple teams have mused whether the Saints would part with beloved franchise icon Alvin Kamara, who has famously stated multiple times he wishes to end his career in New Orleans. “If Mickey (Loomis) comes down and says (they’re trading me), I’m going to go drink a piña colada somewhere,” Kamara said last year around the trade deadline. home.blurb: Sunday’s Week 9 matchup at the Caesars Superdome brings together two teams in very different positions, as the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take the field against the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Cleveland is third in the AFC North but just one game behind the first place Steelers. New Orleans has lost four of their last five games and sit last in the NFC South but they are also only a game out of first as they return from their bye. The Superdome, however, has not been kind to the Saints who are winless in four home games (0-4). Cleveland, however, is a respectable 2-3 on the road this season. New Orleans has not played in a couple weeks, but their last game was also a loss to the Steelers, 16-10, in Paris on Oct. 25. The Saints managed only 18 rushing yards and were shut out in the second half, but quarterback Tyler Shough produced an encouraging performance through the air, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and one interception. It was symptomatic of the season to date: the offense has no balance. Historically, Cleveland leads the all-time series 13-7, but New Orleans has won each of the last three meetings, including the most recent matchup at this same venue on November 17, 2024. That game was tied 14-14 entering the fourth quarter before the Saints exploded for 21 unanswered points to win 35-14. Taysom Hill was the difference-maker, rushing seven times for 138 yards and three touchdowns, including fourth-quarter scoring runs of 33 and 75 yards, while Derek Carr threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns. Jameis Winston threw for 395 yards and two scores for Cleveland, but the Browns failed to turn their yardage into enough points. Two years later, the central question is similar for both clubs: which offense can translate production into touchdowns? Cleveland needs to protect Watson and rediscover a ground game that disappeared in Pittsburgh, while New Orleans needs Shough, Kamara and an offense coming out of the bye to take advantage of a Browns defense that just surrendered 200 rushing yards. home.headline: Saints could get three key players closer to returning to practice
home.blurb: Jordyn Tyson, Travis Etienne Jr. and Kelvin Banks Jr. will all be re-evaluated by the team's medical staff, with the goal of determining whether Wednesday would be an appropriate time for any of them to return to practice. Tyson's potential return would give the Saints another playmaker at wide receiver, and according to ESPN's Adam Schefter , there's a chance he can return as soon as this upcoming week against the Cleveland Browns. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nic Jennings · SB Nation Tue, November 3, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The New Orleans Saints could be getting closer to having several injured players back on the field, with three important names set to undergo evaluations on Monday. Head coach Kellen Moore provided an update on the three players, explaining that their status remains uncertain until they complete additional work with the training staff. "The IR guys still to be determined, they'll have some work today with the training room, and we'll make a decision whether Wednesday's the ideal time to bring them up," Moore said. All three players would be important additions for New Orleans as they look to get healthier for the remainder of the season. However, the Saints are taking a cautious approach rather than rushing anyone back before they are ready. Getting Etienne back is a necessity. The run game has struggled significantly, ultimately leading to the firing of run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti. Having a player like Etienne back in the lineup will be crucial to getting the unit back on track. Meanwhile, getting Banks back would be especially important for an offensive line that needs consistency and stability up front. Asim Richards has struggled with penalties since taking over for Banks, so having one of the league's promising young tackles back in the lineup would be beneficial. For now, Wednesday remains a possibility rather than a guarantee for any of the three players. Monday's evaluations will help determine whether they have progressed enough to take the next step in their respective recoveries. The Saints will have a better idea of where things stand following those evaluations, but the possibility of getting multiple players closer to returning is an encouraging development for a team looking to get healthier down the stretch.

Giants Add Familiar Face at Running Back as Skattebo’s Injury Status Raises Questions Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants were back to work on Monday after their Week 8 bye, but one key offensive player worked with trainers on the sideline during the media portion of practice. Running back Cam Skattebo, who said he felt something in his hamstring after his 42-yard run against the Houston Texans in overtime two weeks ago, was spotted working to the side with trainers. It’s unclear whether Skattebo is simply trying to buy a couple more days to let his hamstring fully heal before the team begins its prep for Sunday’s road game at Philadelphia, or whether the injury could limit him in practice and, potentially, the upcoming game. Head coach John Harbaugh characterized Skattebo's status as "day to day." Either way, the Giants, who last week placed running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR with a hamstring injury, are not taking any chances of going into the critical division matchup with just Devin Singletary and newcomer Gregory Desrosiers, whom they signed last week off the Chargers’ practice squad. To that end, New York has signed running back Eric Gray, its fifth-round pick in the 2023 draft, to its practice squad. Gray, who was with the team this summer, appeared in 34 games over three seasons, including just four in 2025 after landing on PUP due to a knee injury. He has 31 career rushing attempts for 79 yards and caught 16 of 18 targets for 104 yards, with no rushing or receiving touchdowns. This past summer he led the team in receptions with eight catches for 54 yards. He also led the Giants in rushing with 90 yrds on 30 carries. Gray was with the Cleveland Browns practice squad in September but was released in early October. home.blurb: Even after the bye week, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is still dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered during the team's Week 7 overtime win against the Houston Texans. Skattebo did not practice on Monday as the team returned to work. Skattebo broke off a 42-yard run in overtime that helped the Giants pull out a win, but it came at a price, as he picked up a hamstring injury. Giants head coach John Harbaugh spoke about Skattebo's injury in more detail. His struggles led to him being benched in the team's Week 6 loss against the New Orleans Saints, but he redeemed himself against the Texans when he had his best game of the season. He ran 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants pull out a big win on the road. Should Skattebo have to sit out, it will mean an extended opportunity for Devin Singletary and newly-signed Gregory Desrosiers. Eric Gray, who was just signed to the practice squad, and Phil Mafah are running backs who would be available for elevation. home.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
home.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). home.headline: Report: Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw (knee) out for season
home.blurb: He joins fellow defensive tackle Daron Payne (foot) in being out for the season. Payne was placed on IR on Tuesday, four days after he sustained his injury during practice. Nov 04 (Field Level Media) - Washington Commanders defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw will miss the remainder of the season due to a knee injury, ESPN reported Wednesday. Kinlaw, 29, was placed on injured reserve Tuesday after he underwent surgery to repair an MCL injury. He sustained the injury during Washington's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Oct. 19. Kinlaw recorded 13 tackles and one sack in six games (all starts) this season. Signed to a three-year deal prior to the 2025 season, Kinlaw has totaled 166 tackles, 10.5 sacks, three forced fumbles, one fumble recovery and an interception for a touchdown in 81 career games (68 starts) for the 49ers, New York Jets and Commanders. He was selected by San Francisco with the 14th overall pick of the 2020 NFL Draft.

The Washington Commanders have dealt with the injury bug all season long, and things got a bit worse this week following their big win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday night. On Tuesday, the team officially placed defensive tackles Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw, as well as running back Jeremy McNichols, on injured reserve ahead of their matchup against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday. To make matters worse, after already determining that Payne would miss the rest of the season, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Wednesday morning that Kinlaw's stint on injured reserve will also be season-ending. Now in his seventh NFL season and second with the Commanders, Kinlaw left Sunday's game against the Eagles with a knee injury. He will reportedly undergo surgery to repair a torn MCL on Tuesday. “Injury update: Commanders DL Javon Kinlaw underwent season-ending surgery Tuesday on his MCL,” Schefter posted. “Now Commanders defensive linemen Kinlaw and Daron Payne both have suffered season-ending injuries in recent weeks.” Injury update: Commanders DL Javon Kinlaw underwent season-ending surgery Tuesday on his MCL. While he isn't a player who typically fills up the stat sheet, he's been a consistent presence at defensive tackle. The 29-year-old has recorded 13 tackles, 1.0 sack, two tackles for loss, three quarterback hits and two pass deflections at the line of scrimmage this season. Across 81 career games, he's started 67 and totaled 166 tackles, 10.5 sacks and 19 tackles for loss. Kinlaw spent the first four years of his NFL career with the San Francisco 49ers .
