Add ClutchPoints on Google Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Currently 4-4 and third in the NFC West, the 2026 campaign has not gone according to plan for the Los Angeles Rams. However, two straight wins have put the Rams right back in the thick of the playoff race. With two road games coming up against the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals, Los Angeles received some promising news. ESPN insider Adam Schefter shared Rams head coach Sean McVay's updates on star edge rusher Myles Garrett and tight end Terrance Ferguson via X, formerly Twitter. “Help is on the way: Myles Garrett will practice this week, and Terrance Ferguson might,” Schefter reposted Monday evening. Acquired this offseason, Garrett was supposed to team up with the returning Aaron Donald to cause havoc in the backfields of the Rams' opponents. However, after a quiet debut in the Rams' Week 1 loss to division rival San Francisco in Australia, Garrett hit the IR. The fact that he'll be able to get back on the field for practice is a massive boost for Los Angeles. If Garrett gets back to the form that helped him break the NFL single season sack record last fall, then he will be a massive headache for the upcoming teams on LA's schedule. Getting Ferguson back should help the offense as well. The unit has been inconsistent at times, but it has improved in the last two wins. With star receiver Davante Adams on the shelf, and Puka Nacua routinely battling some ailment, having Ferguson team up with veteran Tyler Higbee will only help signal caller Matthew Stafford. With wins over the Commanders and the Cardinals over the next two weeks, the Rams could truly be back in contention. Getting both Garrett and Ferguson back on the field should only help Los Angeles going forward. Jordan Llanes is a sports writer and reporter based in Florida. home.headline: Injuries beginning to take their toll on the Panthers' secondary, offensive line
home.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
home.blurb: “Just wanna see the guys connected,” Panthers coach Dave Canales said. "I just wanna see them excited about going out there and executing the plan. And playing fast, playing the physical brand. And the effort’s been there. Those things are right. But I know that we can make strides with being able to get everybody on the same page, tying in the whole unit.” Moton, the team's longtime right tackle, was able to return to action three weeks ago, but since injured his fibula and has been placed on injured reserve. Ekwonu is expected back in the next month or so. CHARLOTTE, N.C. (AP) — The Carolina Panthers are probably wishing they could petition the NFL for another bye week. Mounting injuries to the secondary and offensive line have begun to take their toll on the Panthers (3-4), who have dropped two straight games and fallen into a tie with the Atlanta Falcons for first place in the NFC South. On Friday, the Panthers fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero after the team allowed Jordan Love to throw for 288 yards and three touchdowns in a 27-19 loss to the Green Bay Packers. Carolina entered the game last in the league in run defense. The Panthers promoted defensive line coach Todd Wash as interim defensive coordinator. Evero's fate may have been sealed when starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson went down in a Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns and were placed on injured reserve. Since then, the two cornerbacks who were replaced Horn and Jackson have suffered injuries. Akayleb Evans was placed on IR last week and Will Lee injured his hamstring against the Packers in the first half and had to leave the game. Canales said the injuries were taken into account when he fired Evero, but added that the decision was based on the big picture and “a lot of information." Things are just as shaky on the offensive line where the Panthers are playing without three starters, including tackles Taylor Moton and Ickey Ekwonu and guard Damien Lewis. Bryce Young was under constant pressure against the Packers. He was hurried 22 times, hit nine times and sacked six times. “We’ve got to make sure we do a good job of giving him solutions when they do have overloaded pressures and zero looks and things," Canales said. "But it wasn’t just that. They got after us with some four-man rushes and some stunts that we didn’t pass off well. That created a little bit of pressure there as well.” Rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has struggled at right tackle this season. Running back Chuba Hubbard continues to be a bright spot for the Panthers despite playing behind an offensive line that has struggled to open holes. Hubbard was used extensively against the Packers and gained 81 yards on 22 carries while hauling in a team-high seven passes for 38 yards. He's clearly the only back offensive coordinator Brad Idzik trusts at this point in the season. away.headline: Tank Dell on serving as Texans' punt returner after Jaylin Noel's injury
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Houston Texans ultimately lost to the New York Giants , but it was a win to see wide receiver Tank Dell return to the field after nearly two years. He finished the game with two rushing yards, a 43-yard reception and a punt return for 14 yards. Through most of this season, Jaylin Noel served as Houston’s punt returner. However, Dell got the opportunity to return a punt after Noel suffered a toe injury. Unfortunately for Houston, Noel will miss the remainder of the season with turf toe. So, it appears Dell may have to step up as the Texans’ punt returner for the rest of the season. Even though that is not something he has typically done in the NFL, he does have some collegiate experience returning punts. Luckily, Dell has extra time to practice at punt returner during the bye week before Houston’s next game against the winless Los Angeles Chargers. However, it will be a difficult matchup since the Chargers have only allowed an average of 8.9 yards per punt return this season. Houston has also struggled in the punt return game with an average of only nine yards per return, which is No. 20 in the NFL. "Very comfortable. I've been catching punts since college,” Dell said. “I'm very comfortable back there fielding the ball, making guys miss and getting up field and try to break a touchdown. I haven't done one of those yet, so that's what I'm looking forward to." This article originally appeared on Texans Wire: Tank Dell on serving as Texans' punt returner after Jaylin Noel's injury

away.headline: Houston Texans WR Jaylin Noel will miss rest of the season with turf toe injury
away.blurb: The injury is a major blow, not only for the Texans, but also for Noel, who was having a breakout year. He was leading the team with 331 receiving yards. He has 19 catches, two receiving touchdowns and served as the team's primary return man. The timetable for an athlete's return depends on the extent of the tear. A player can recover from a Grade 1 turf toe injury after weeks with rest. The Texans were hoping that was the case, but further tests showed that it was more significant than that, the source said. For Noel to need surgery on the toe, it likely means he suffered a Grade 3 turf toe, which will take months to heal and will keep him out for the remainder of the season. Dell can play out of the slot similarly to Noel, where he starred during his first two NFL seasons before the injury. Last week's game against the Giants was Dell's first time playing in a game in nearly two years. He had one catch for 43 yards and a 2-yard run on limited snaps. The 43-yard catch was a big one, as it led to a touchdown a few plays later. The Texans could also utilize Xavier Hutchinson in the slot. Hutchinson is not the same downfield threat as Noel and Dell, but he has had his most success as a receiver out of the slot. Houston Texans wide receiver Jaylin Noel is expected to miss the rest of the season and undergo surgery on his toe, a person with knowledge of the injury told the Chronicle. Noel was placed on injured reserve because of turf toe, the team announced Wednesday afternoon. The Texans selected Noel in the third round of the 2025 NFL draft, and his emergence had become a major breakthrough for an offense that has continued to find its way through seven weeks. The Texans rank fourth in the NFL in passing yards and second in pass plays of 20 yards or more, in large part because of Noel's explosiveness. Houston will miss that significantly. Noel appeared to suffer the injury with 8:47 left in the fourth quarter of Sunday's loss to the Giants. Noel was returning a kick and as he was brought down, his toe twisted on the turf. Noel never returned to the game and was seen in a walking boot afterward. Turf toe is an injury to the big toe joint when ligaments, tendons and soft tissues in the joint stretch or tear, according to the Cleveland Clinic . The injury is common among football players who sprint and jump. It happens when the toe remains on the ground and the heel lifts, causing the toe to hyperextend. The Texans do have depth at receiver after recently trading for Marvin Harrison Jr . They also got Tank Dell back from a significant knee injury last week. "You guys know me, I'm ready to the role," Dell said after Sunday's game. "I've been in the role to be that guy already. You all know how it gets, so I'm ready for it." In the secondary, it is going to be interesting to see if Jackson and Shelly are going to be able to play because the Rams have a great receiver in the form of Puka Nacua, who can take advantage if the secondary is not ready to play. On the offensive side, having Harris and McConkey being on track to be in the lineup for Sunday could be huge for quarterback Justin Herbert and the offense to get on track in the passing game which is something that the offense has been unable to do all year thus far. All that said, the Chargers are in a solid position health wise heading into this matchup against the Rams, so it will ultimately come downs to which team executes better between the Chargers and the Rams.

picks.headline: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9
picks.blurb: Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Packers vs. Patriots bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:49 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is one of the most interesting and compelling games of the schedule for Week 9 and the first half of the NFL season. The Green Bay Packers are starting to find their offensive rhythm with Jordan Love improving on a week-by-week basis, but the team is still waiting for Micah Parsons to return to help the defense assert itself. The New England Patriots are in full stride at the moment. After losing two of their first three games and looking like last year's Super Bowl champions might take a step or two backwards, the Patriots have found their stride once again. It certainly begins with Drake Maye , who is starting to make a case as one of the NFL's elite quarterbacks, but it goes much deeper than that. The Patriots have been getting excellent play from their offensive line and running back Rhamondre Stevenson is one of the most dependable players that head coach Mike Vrabel has on his roster. His presence is a security blanket to the rest of the team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the Patriots are feeling better about themselves on an every-week basis, the defense is also getting the job done. New England ranks 9th in scoring defense , as the Patriots are giving up 20.3 points per game. However, the Packers may be encouraged when they look at the New England pass defense because that unit is only slightly better than average, ranking 13th in the league. Jordan Love will throw for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns The Packers would like to come at the Patriots with a balanced, versatile and unpredictable attack. The return of Josh Jacobs from the commissioner's exempt list gave head coach Matt LaFleur a solid option running the ball. However, recent allegations of additional domestic violence incidents against Jacobs could result in additional discipline by the NFL. While he is still eligible at this moment, LaFleur might want to bypass that portion of the gameplan. As a result, it will be on Love to direct a consistent offensive attack, and he will be under significant pressure from the Patriots' aggressive defense. Love is one of the best pure passers in the game, and if the offensive line gives him protection, he can drive the Green Bay attack. Love has completed 192 of 312 passes for 2,246 yards and is averaging 280.8 yards per game. He has thrown 16 TD passes and 6 interceptions. He has a trio of receivers who are likely to cause problems in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and TE Tucker Kraft. Watson's speed, route running and dependable hands should help the Patriots stay in this vital road game. Look for Love to connect with Watson for at least one key touchdown in the fourth quarter. Maye will approach 225 passing yards and 2 touchdowns Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Look for Maye to be turned on to the maximum level for this matchup with Love. He knows that Love throws one of the best deep balls in the league, and Maye wants to compete with him in all areas. While Love is also a good runner who can escape the pass rush, Maye excels in that area. Look for Maye to show off those running skill early in the game, and that will force the Packers to employ a spy who will attempt to contain the quarterback. That's when Maye will start to show off his pinpoint passing. The Patriots quarterback has completed 157 of 234 passes for 1,983 yards with 15 touchdowns and 8 interceptions. In addition to those numbers, his confidence is sky high. While the Patriots have not gotten the production from former Eagles wideout A.J. Brown, he can depend on wide receiver DeMario Douglas and tight end Hunter Henry to show off their productivity against Green Bay's eighth-ranked pass defense. Stevenson will rush for 75-plus yards and 1 TD The Patriots have one of the most underrated running backs in the game in Rhamondre Stevenson. While he is not a gamebreaker in terms of speed, he understands all aspects of the game. He runs well between the tackles and he will finish off his rushing attempts with power. He knows how to set up his blockers and accelerate at the right moment. The Patriots have TreVeyon Henderson — when healthy — to show off his skills as a speed back. However, it is Stevenson who is a difference maker and will give the Patriots the edge they need to beat a solid opponent. Patriots will outlast Packers and earn 27-24 triumph The escape factor that Maye provides will allow him to buy extra time and create more plays for the Patriots. This will allow them to maintain possession and sustain their drives. He will also get a huge lift from Stevenson, who is simply a winner and will come through when the game is on the line. The Packers will push the Patriots to the limit, but the Pats will have the benefit of their homefield, as well as their two key difference makers. New England comes away with this exciting and well-played victory. picks.blurb: The Patriots are likely to be on A.J. Brown watch once again. After the receiver missed Sunday's win over the Dolphins with a knee injury, Mike Vrabel said Monday that the team would need to see how Brown progresses before determinig his status for the upcoming tilt. Micah Parsons is expected to make his much-anticipated return to practice this week for the Packers, but he might still be a long way out from contributing. Matt LaFleur said the edge rusher might need the full 21-day window before being added to the active roster, which would mean a late November return. If there is any change to running back Josh Jacobs' disciplinary status, it won't come from the Packers. LaFleur said this week that the team plans to continue on with the ball carrier as the NFL extends its investigation. Patriots vs Packers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Patriots -3.5 Moneyline: Patriots -160; Packers +145 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Patriots vs Packers USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Patriots 24, Packers 23 The Patriots are 17-0 with Drake Maye when favored by at least a field goal and we just may close there by Sunday afternoon. Who am I to disagree with a great trend? The Packers possess a dynamic passing offense but, even with Josh Jacobs back, still can't run the football with any efficiency. Plus, Christian Watson is dealing with a rib injury that sent him to the hospital for a portion of last week's primetime win over the Panthers. The Pats have the personnel to take advantage defensively, but Maye's offense also has questions around injuries to A.J. Brown, Hunter Henry and others. I'll take New England at home, but I'm expecting nervous pacing around living rooms throughout Massachusetts before this one is settled. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Packers 28, Patriots 27 Bombs away. With a matchup of two daring downfield passers and lackluster run games, both teams could air it out early and often against one another. Between their reliance on Jordan Love connecting on vertical shots and the pass rush picking up the rest of the defense with pressure, Green Bay might be more reliant of the two on igniting big plays. But the Packers' explosiveness shouldn't be doubted, and it could lead the team to its fifth win in six games. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 26, Patriots 23 Good luck figuring these teams out. At times, Green Bay looks like a bad team. Then it looks like a Super Bowl contender. The same is true of New England, meaning there is a large range of outcomes we could see in Week 9. Will A.J. Brown play for the Patriots? Does it matter? Drop issues have plagued the star receiver and there's no sign of that disappearing anytime soon. On the other side, Christian Watson made 'Thursday Night Football” look like the WWE with his dramatic return. In the end, we'll trust the Packers offense to be the difference. picks.blurb: Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:56 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Las Vegas Raiders arrive at Levi's Stadium with renewed confidence. The San Francisco 49ers arrive with extra rest and something to prove. Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a 38–33 victory over the Jets, improving to 4–4. San Francisco, meanwhile, returns from its bye at 6–1 after suffering its first defeat, a 29–20 loss to Atlanta. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brock Purdy throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Purdy will deliver his most convincing statistical statement of the season, reaching 350 passing yards and throwing four touchdown passes. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. home.headline: NFL Fans Clown on Brandon Aiyuk After 49ers Star Appeals to Be Reinstated After Ditching Franchise
home.blurb: Earlier this offseason, wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk promised that he wouldn't return to the San Francisco 49ers ' building this season. And even if he returns, that would be on October 19, 2026, when the Niners will host the Washington Commanders , the receiver's preferred destination to play in the 2026 season. San Fran hosted Washington and defeated them 23-17. Aiyuk, however, wasn't signed by the Commanders. Aiyuk's decision came almost a year after the 49ers placed him on the reserve/left squad list on December 13, 2025. To return to the 49ers, Aiyuk was supposed to apply for reinstatement. But amid his fallout with the franchise, the receiver had no intention of doing so. "I will not be reinstated with them or ever doing any kind of business with them," a frustrated Aiyuk said in a social media post in July. "I'm locked in and focused on my opportunity to return to the field this season." That opportunity, however, didn't come, as Aiyuk now expects to return to the same building he said he had no plans to show up to. Certainly, the receiver's decision drew significant criticism, as NFL fans took a dig at Brandon Aiyuk for his interest in playing for the 49ers again after criticising the team for months. "Bro submitted a permission slip to show up to his own job.????," one person wrote, while another pointed out, "I'm sorry. I truly forgot he played for the 49ers because of how good they have been without him." Aiyuk's decision comes at a time when the 49ers need receiver help following Mike Evans' injury. As Aiyuk's appeal for reinstatement gained traction, 49ers reporter Grant Cohn said he would like to see both sides work things out, especially with San Francisco in contention for the Super Bowl. "Wouldn't it be a great story if they worked it out after all this, he came back, played well, and was a big figure on this team down the stretch? It would be huge. Iggy, imagine this: They go to the Super Bowl. It's Super Bowl week, he's on the team, and he's helped bring them to the Super Bowl. He would be a media story." But the deal turned out to be a total bust, as Aiyuk suffered a significant knee injury, ruling him out for the rest of the 2024 season. The expectation was that Aiyuk would rehabilitate the injury and eventually return to the 49ers during the 2025 season. But the return never happened. Aiyuk remained on the physically unable to perform list throughout the 2025 season as he recovered from the knee injury. While the 49ers remained optimistic that he would return at some point during the season, things went downhill after Aiyuk reportedly stopped reporting to the team facility and failed to participate in meetings and other team activities. Subsequently, Aiyuk identified the Commanders as his preferred destination. He also made it clear that he wanted the 49ers to release him rather than continue holding his contractual rights. Now, though, with the off-field issues and questions surrounding his desire and want to get back on the field, the market may have disappeared. The Washington Commanders were once thought to be 100 percent committed to acquiring Aiyuk, but reports have indicated that Washington will no longer be involved in the Aiyuk sweepstakes if/when he becomes available. San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk hasn't caught a pass in an NFL game since Oct. 20, 2024. Just months after signing a four-year, $120 million contract extension, Aiyuk suffered a torn ACL and MCL that caused him to miss the remainder of the 2024 season. Brandon Aiyuk has filed for reinstatement According to ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter, Aiyuk has turned in paperwork to be reinstated . When that happens, Aiyuk will force the 49ers' hand in making a roster move. San Francisco will either have to keep, trade or release Aiyuk. It has been made clear multiple times by the 49ers organization that Aiyuk is not a part of their plans, meaning that being released or eventually traded is likely what will happen. Is there still a market for Brandon Aiyuk? At one point in time, even after the injuries, there were still teams that would've been interested in Aiyuk. In his last full season before the ACL tear, Aiyuk posted 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns. It will be intriguing to see if anyone is willing to take a chance on Aiyuk after a two-year absence. away.headline: Report: Lions will ink former Cardinals, Titans LB to practice squad
away.blurb: Head coach Dan Campbell was asked earlier this week how the coaching staff plans to prepare, if Campbell is out for the foreseeable future. "So, we may need a little bit of help. We're looking at everything. We'll adjust as we go. (Lions Executive Vice President and General Manager) Brad (Holmes) and I will get together here this afternoon, tomorrow and figure some of this out.” After visiting the Detroit Lions Allen Park Performance Center, a decision was made on former Arizona Cardinals, Tennessee Titans linebacker Owen Pappoe. According to multiple reports, the 26-year-old will ink a deal to join Detroit's practice squad. Detroit's linebackers unit was in need of added depth this week after two players went down against the Minnesota Vikings with significant injuries. Rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder was lost for the remainder of the 2026 season due to a hamstring injury. Captain Jack Campbell is still hospitalized after a frightening neck injury suffered in the second half of a 19-15 Week 8 victory against a division rival. According to an Athletic scouting report , "The Tigers’ two-year captain ran the fastest combine 40 (4.39) among the linebackers. The 6-foot, 225-pounder isn’t particularly big, but was an effective leader/communicator in the middle of the Auburn defense who should benefit as a run-and-chase, weakside linebacker at the next level. Pappoe had a pair of 90-tackle seasons at Auburn." Additional Detroit Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Grading Week 8 Victory Against Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field “Well, luckily we have some depth in there with (Malcolm Rodriguez) Rodrigo and (Trevor) Nowaske and (Derrick) Barnes. Those three guys and (Lions LB) Amen (Ogbongbemiga)’s been up for us, which is good," said the sixth-year NFL head man. "And then we have got (Joe) Bachie ready to roll. The roster has been regularly updated regarding Campbell's current health status. “Well, I think we acknowledge it, right? I mean, it's not going away," said Campbell. "That is what it is and it's important. And he's important to us and that he's okay is important. And so we acknowledge that, we talk about it and at the same time we get ready for this next opponent. Zach Charbonnet is expected to make his season debut versus the Chicago Bears , and although he is still on injured reserve at time of print, rookie Jadarian Price is in line to join him. Even without Kyle Monangai, who is still battling turf toe and a thumb injury, the Bears boast a dangerous D'Andre Swift-led rushing unit. Chicago has not lost a game that Williams has started and finished this season (4-0), and it upset the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8. The Bears have also scored at least 30 points in every game that Williams has completed this season, making them one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. Oddsmakers have set Chicago as a six-point favorite at home as it looks to get to 7-2 before a Week 10 bye. The Bears are still behind the 6-1 Minnesota Vikings – who beat them earlier this season – in the NFC North standings. Let’s take a look at the opening odds for this primetime matchup in a loaded Week 9. This is a battle between two very different teams, as Tampa Bay has relied heavily on the running game and its defense to get back in the playoff mix while the Bears are one of the best offenses in football. Chicago ranks 10th in EPA/Play, 11th in success rate and tied for 13th in yards per play this season despite the fact that Williams has missed three full games and part of the team’s Week 2 loss to Minnesota. When the former No. 1 overall pick has been on the field, Ben Johnson’s club has been humming on the offensive end, dropping 34 points in Week 8 against a Seattle defense that is No. 1 in the NFL in success rate and entered Week 8 at No. 1 in yards per play allowed. Tampa Bay’s defense is now No. 1 in EPA/Play after picking off Michael Penix Jr. several times in a rain-soaked matchup in Week 8, but things won’t be nearly as easy against Williams. On the bright side for the Bucs, they should be able to run the ball (eighth in EPA/Rush this season) against a Bears defense that is allowing 4.4 yards per carry in 2026. Chicago traded for star defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons ahead of Week 8, but the Tampa Bay running game – led by Bucky Irving – won’t be easy to stop on Sunday night. I lean with the Bears to win this game, and it’ll be interesting to see if the odds move at all with both teams trending in the right direction with the halfway point of the 2026 season upon us. If Chicago leads by two scores in the third quarter, Tampa Bay has to abandon the run and put the ball in Mayfield's hands. I expect two interceptions, including one that sets up a Chicago touchdown. The Bucs will compete. They'll move the ball, their kicker has been perfect this season and their defense will make a few plays. away.headline: Buccaneers get a major boost from latest injury report ahead of Week 8 vs. Falcons
away.blurb: Fortunately, the Buccaneers received some encouraging news on the injury front just in time for the pivotal matchup. Several key players are trending toward a return, giving Tampa Bay a chance to take the field with its healthiest roster in weeks. The Buccaneers released their injury report after practice on Thursday, and several designations stood out. Antoine Winfield Jr. was a full participant after missing the last three games with a fractured rib , and the star safety is gearing up for a return. Heading into a matchup against a stacked Falcons offense featuring Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Kyle Pitts, the importance of Winfield's return can't be overstated. Emeka Egbuka, who missed last week due to a concussion and foot injury, was a limited participant and has a chance to play against the Falcons. But Irving and Godwin were each given rest days, so Goedeke is the only player truly out with an injury as things currently stand. All in all, it’s hard not to be encouraged with Winfield making his return and Egbuka having a chance to do the same. Both teams will be overwhelmingly healthy entering Week 8, so there are no excuses. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers’ showdown with the Atlanta Falcons in Week 8 will make or break the season, and the Bucs need all hands on deck to keep their playoff hopes alive. Buccaneers get encouraging injury news at the perfect time ahead of Falcons showdown Josiah Trotter, who missed practice earlier in the week due to an illness, returned as a full particplant on Thursday. Kenny Gainwell, coming off his best game as a Buccaneer with 88 rushing yards, returned to practice after missing Wednesday with a hip injury. Tampa Bay is getting healthy at the perfect time. Luke Goedeke could be Buccaneers' only key absence in Week 8 The only three players who didn’t practice were Luke Goedeke, Bucky Irving and Chris Godwin Jr. While being without their premier starting right tackle is far from ideal, the Bucs’ offense operated just fine with Benjamin Chukwuma as the starting right tackle last week. In fact, it was their best performance of the year, allowing zero sacks and rushing for 258 total yards. Todd Bowles went on the record saying that Chukwuma has a “huge future” as an NFL starter , so the coaching staff has the utmost confidence in him as the next-man up. away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their initial injury report Wednesday ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, with three players sitting out practice and two others participating on a limited basis. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who continues to deal with concussion and foot injuries, was limited in practice. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also limited due to an illness. Atlanta also opened the week with several players sidelined. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not participate in practice. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith was also held out for rest. The Falcons had six players listed as limited participants, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), defensive linemen LaCale London (chest) and Charles Snowden (back), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring), cornerback Avieon Terrell (illness) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. picks.headline: Bills at Vikings: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 9 game
picks.blurb: Two 6-1 teams, one marquee matchup. The Bills visit Minnesota after beating the Ravens 36-10, while the Vikings look to rebound from their first loss, a 19-15 defeat in Detroit. Kyler Murray's hamstring is the biggest injury to watch. Kevin O'Connell said Murray remained under evaluation Monday. Carson Wentz is the next option if Murray cannot play but, even if he starts, his mobility deserves attention. Wentz guided the Vikings to wins over the Packers and Bears in September, completing 59% of his passes with three touchdowns and no interceptions. Minnesota's protection is another concern. Left tackle Christian Darrisaw is dealing with shoulder soreness. His availability becomes especially important if Murray's hamstring limits his ability to escape pressure. Josh Allen's supporting cast needs monitoring, too. Joshua Palmer injured his hamstring against Baltimore, DJ Moore picked up another injury concern, and right tackle Spencer Brown missed that game with a back issue. Their practice participation will matter this week. The early market favors Buffalo on the road. The Bills are favorites of -3/-3.5 points, depending on where you do your shopping, and the total has dropped from 48.5 at open to as low as 45.5. Murray's status could move both numbers. If you're curious to read a couple of interesting trends: The Vikings are a perfect 7-0 SU and ATS in the fourth quarter this season, while the Bills are 6-0-1 SU and 7-0 ATS in the second quarter. These are shocking stats when you consider the teams are a combined 12-2 on the year, but just thought we'd pass it along. Vikings vs Bills odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Bills -3.5 Moneyline: Bills -170; Vikings +155 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Vikings vs Bills USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Bills 24, Vikings 20 Do we have a Super Bowl preview on our hands? Guess that depends how you feel about Minnesota's offense and Buffalo's defense. Either way, we've got a pair of 6-1 teams, a few superstar talents in Josh Allen, James Cook and Justin Jefferson, plus a banged up Kyler Murray with a hamstring injury that could move the line before kickoff. Whether it's Murray or Carson Wentz stepping in for him again, I still trust the Bills more to manufacture points. Brian Flores and the Vikings defense will make Allen work for everything – as the Lions just experienced in their low-scoring win – but the visitors simply have more at their disposal and I like them to remain unbeaten on the road. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Bills 21, Vikings 14 For a team that was the league's last undefeated group standing, the Vikings are facing quite a bit of strife. A rickety offense might soon become fully broken if Kyler Murray continues to miss on downfield opportunities. Jim Leonhard's defense has hardly been a bunch of world-beaters, but the opportunistic group continues to come up with big plays in key moments, particularly with its pass rush. If the Bills can get Murray off schedule, it could be a difficult evening for Minnesota. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Vikings 21, Bills 16 Offense or defense? Like Week 8, the Vikings find themselves in a matchup that features strength vs. strength and weakness vs. weakness. It was the Lions offense that triumphed against the Vikings defense, but there's reason to believe things could be different this week. Buffalo has been much looser with the football this year, turning it over 11 times – which ranks 11th-most in the league, while Detroit has the third-fewest. Suddenly, you see the Vikings' path to victory. Brian Flores' defense forces Josh Allen into a mistake or two on Monday night and that is the difference. home.blurb: #Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said QB Kyler Murray is dealing with a sore hamstring, and he'll have a full evaluation. Murray seemed limited at the end of Sunday's game. Since the Vikings don't play until Monday, they aren't scheduled to release an injury report from practice until Thursday. Kyler Murray Injury Update Causes Minor Shift to Vikings' Odds vs. Bills in NFL Week 9 Skip to main content ON SI Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray suffered a hamstring issue in Week 8 of the 2026 season, as the team lost to the Detroit Lions. According to Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell, Murray has a "sore" hamstring and will have a full evaluation before the team resumes practice this week. The Vikings don't play until Monday night against the Buffalo Bills in Week 9, so Murray will have an extra day to get healthy. If Murray is unable to go in Week 9, the Vikings would turn to veteran Carson Wentz at quarterback. Since Minnesota traded away former first-round pick J.J. McCarthy, Wentz and Max Brosmer are the only two remaining quarterbacks on the roster. DraftKings Sportbsook had moved the Vikings to 2.5-point underdogs at home in this matchup, but the line has since shifted back up to Minnesota +3.5. The Vikings opened as three-point underdogs on Sunday night , but they were gaining ground at home before the Murray update was released. Clearly, the betting market is bracing for the former No. 1 overall pick potentially missing Monday's matchup. This season, Murray has completed 64.9 percent of his passes for 1,022 yards, five scores and three picks while adding 29 carries for 167 yards on the ground. He was banged up early in the season with a concussion, leading to Wentz playing the majority of the team's first two games against Green Bay and Chicago. The Vikings' offense has not been good in the 2026 season, ranking 30th in the league in EPA/Play and 31st in success rate. However, elite play by the team's defense has kept it in first place in the NFC North at 6-1. For now, the betting market isn't reacting too much ahead of this marquee matchup on Monday night. home.blurb: Buffalo selected defensive tackle Zane Durant in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft out of Penn State. He was expected to be a depth option for Buffalo, but he's been out injured. "I've seen him out at practice; he's in a jersey, no pads, and he's still on injured reserve. The Buffalo Bills are unlikely to get back a rookie defensive player anytime soon. The Bills are off to a 6-1 start and will play the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football. Buffalo Bills Get Injury Update on Zane Durant In preseason and training camp, Durant flashed his potential, and many fans thought he would make an impact. However, Durant was placed on injured reserve at the end of August due to a neck stinger. He's been on the practice field, but Bills insider Matt Parrino of NYUP.com said he wasn't sure if Durant gets activated this year. Durant played four years at Penn State and was a big part of their defense. In his final season, he recorded 25 tackles, 4 sacks, and an interception . The Bills' defense has been an issue this season, but on Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens , they looked much better. After watching back the tape, Bills head coach Joe Brady said that is how the defense is expected to play every week. "I think our defense should look at today and understand that that's what the expectation is," Brady said . "And I'm not talking about the production. I'm not talking about the takeaways and sacks. home.headline: Vikings-Lions Final Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions' injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday's game, which means he's likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he's likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR.
